Wellcome priority themes

This analysis uses existing GBD classifications as a proxy for alignment with Wellcome's specified research priorities within Infectious Diseases and Mental Health. The findings provide an indicative rather than comprehensive characterisation of thematic alignment. About the thematic mapping

Explore individual themes

Publications coded to any GBD 2023 infectious cause: HIV/AIDS and sexually transmitted infections; respiratory infections and tuberculosis; enteric infections; neglected tropical diseases and malaria; other infectious diseases; and infections where the disease is not stated. GBD codes each study to the condition its intervention prevents or treats, so cross-cutting work such as vaccines or drug-resistant infection is captured only where it targets an infectious cause.

Definition and matching criteria
  • Eligible GBD 2023 groups:
    HIV/AIDS and sexually transmitted infectionsRespiratory infections and tuberculosisEnteric infectionsNeglected tropical diseases and malariaOther infectious diseasesInfections, disease not stated
  • Rationale: Wellcome's Infectious Disease priority, represented by the previously agreed GBD infectious cause groups.
  • Limitations: GBD codes the condition an intervention prevents or treats (HPV vaccination under cervical cancer, hepatitis C treatment under chronic liver disease), and cannot separately identify vaccines, drug-resistant infection or epidemic preparedness. “Infections, disease not stated” is a team coding group flagged for review: 676 publications are in this theme only through it (1 Wellcome-funded).
  • GBD codes were assigned from titles and abstracts under the team's coding rules and checked against a second coder and MeSH headings; they were not reviewed publication by publication. Full methodology

Wellcome's specified focus within mental health: anxiety, depression and psychosis, represented by the GBD 2023 causes depressive disorders, anxiety disorders, schizophrenia and bipolar disorder (Wellcome's funding calls list bipolar disorder among psychotic disorders). Other mental disorders and substance use disorders are not included. Wellcome's emphasis on early intervention cannot be identified from GBD codes.

Definition and matching criteria
  • Eligible GBD 2023 level-3 causes:
    Depressive disordersAnxiety disordersSchizophreniaBipolar disorder
  • Rationale: Wellcome's stated focus on anxiety, depression and psychosis (Wellcome: Mental Health). GBD has no psychosis cause; schizophrenia and bipolar disorder represent it, bipolar disorder because Wellcome's funding calls list it among psychotic disorders (example call).
  • Limitations: other mental disorders, substance use disorders and publications coded only to “Mental disorders” without a specific condition are not included. Early intervention cannot be identified from GBD codes.
  • GBD codes were assigned from titles and abstracts under the team's coding rules and checked against a second coder and MeSH headings; they were not reviewed publication by publication. Full methodology

Wellcome-funded evidence across the HEE map

This section covers every publication in the map, whatever its topic.

174publications with Wellcome identified as a funder, of 41,610 in the map (2010–2026)

Coverage of the GBD-based thematic mapping

57%43%
Captured by thematic mapping: 99 (56.9% of 174)Not captured by thematic mapping: 75 (43.1% of 174)

The thematic analysis provides an indicative characterisation of the HEE evidence base using existing GBD classifications as a proxy for Wellcome's specified research priorities. Differences in the scope and granularity of these classification systems limit the extent to which thematic alignment can be captured.

Wellcome-funded publications not captured by this mapping may nevertheless contribute to Wellcome's research priorities, including through cross-cutting research and areas not represented by the selected GBD categories. The results should therefore not be interpreted as a comprehensive assessment of Wellcome's research portfolio or its alignment with strategic priorities.

Other Wellcome-funded HEE publications (75)

Wellcome-funded publications not captured by the GBD-based priority mapping, with the GBD code each was given. The first group is defined by GBD codes; the others are formed from keywords in the titles and are indicative. Select a group to list its publications.

Vaccines, hepatitis C and antibiotic use11

GBD 2023 classifies each study under the condition its intervention prevents or treats, shown beside each title: HPV vaccination under cervical cancer, hepatitis C treatment under cirrhosis and other chronic liver diseases, maternal Group B strep vaccination under neonatal disorders, antibiotic prophylaxis in miscarriage surgery under maternal disorders, and an antibiotic stewardship programme under no single disease. These are not GBD infectious causes, so these publications are not captured by the GBD-based Infectious Diseases mapping.

Wellcome-funded publications by publication year

All 174 Wellcome-funded publications. Publication counts, not grant-award dates or spending.

The annual view uses a fixed 0–100 scale with gridlines every 30 publications; the cumulative view has its own scale. Hover the chart, or focus it and use the arrow keys, for exact counts. 2026 is a partial year (searches ended 3 August 2026), shown with a dashed final segment and hollow point; its lower count does not indicate a decline.

Methodology and limitations

Crosswalk: specified priority areas and eligible GBD codes

Eligibility was fixed from the previously agreed specifications before funding results were calculated, and the same criteria apply to every publication whoever funds it. Wellcome funding was not used to decide eligibility.

Scope exclusions

  • Other mental disorders and substance use disorders: Previously counted in the broad Mental Health theme (v5/v6); outside Wellcome's specified focus, so not eligible here.
  • 'Mental disorders' with no level-3 condition coded: Cannot be assigned to anxiety, depression or psychosis; not eligible. Flagged for review.
  • Climate & Health: Identified by a reviewed keyword screen, not GBD codes; excluded from every displayed analysis and aggregate.
  • 17 Wellcome-funded publications added on title-and-abstract review (v6): Identified only by supplementary screening of Wellcome-funded publications; excluded.

200 publications coded only to “Mental disorders” (1 Wellcome-funded) are among those not eligible.

Why a publication may not be captured

Non-matching may reflect GBD classification limitations, cross-cutting research, the exclusion of Climate & Health, the exclusion of publications identified only through supplementary screening, or research in other areas. These reasons have not been systematically assessed; non-matching does not imply that a publication lacks thematic relevance.

Verification versus supplementary identification

Publications that meet the GBD criteria are included whether or not their coding was also checked by hand. Publications found only through supplementary searches or manual screening, such as the 17 Wellcome-funded publications added on review in the previous version, are excluded, so every funder's publications are identified in the same way.

Unit of analysis and deduplication

The unit is a unique eligible publication (one record ID), not a grant, funding amount or funder mention. Combined figures count each publication once even when it is captured by both themes (9 publications, 0 of them Wellcome-funded). Breakdown groups can overlap and are labelled where they do.

Funding identification and missingness

Funders come from Crossref publication metadata; titles and abstracts were screened, not full texts. A funder is identified for 26.8% of all 41,610 publications (11,149). “Funder not identified” means none was found in the metadata, not that the publication was unfunded. A publication is Wellcome-funded when Wellcome Trust is among its identified funders, alone or with others (Burroughs Wellcome Fund is a separate funder). Funder names are lightly normalised (NIHR, HTA, NIH, MRC, Gates and common variants) and counted once per publication.

Multiple funders and rankings

A publication may report several funders and counts towards each, so funder counts do not sum to the theme total. Ranks use competition ranking: tied funders share a rank. Rankings compare publication counts, not funding amounts.

Country income groups

Single-country publications use the World Bank income group in force on 1 January of the publication year. Multi-country, regional and global publications, and single-country publications whose income group is unavailable, form a third group.

Publication years

Publications from 2010 to 3 August 2026, when searches ended; 2026 is therefore partial. The annual trend uses a fixed 0–100 axis with ticks every 30, so that year-to-year differences are not visually exaggerated; exact counts are given on hover.

What publication counts can and cannot show

Publication counts describe the economic evidence in the map and the funders it acknowledges. They do not measure funding amounts, expenditure, grant portfolios or strategic performance, and the map covers economic evidence (including reviews) rather than all research Wellcome funds.
